cases.name: Bobbie Jo Thomas
cases.about:
(Her daughter Darian) Spiker and others wanted people to know the good in her mom; her troubles, mostly with drugs, did not define her. Bubbly, she was talented and artistic, and made sure her six children were safe, even if they were not with her.

"She was a loving, caring person, but she didn't know how to deal with the demons," Spiker said.

Thomas had such compassion, said (friend, Hoss) Stevens, who met Thomas at a bar, on a Tuesday night about 20 years ago. "The one thing everyone has missed: she had a huge heart and she was very loyal to her friends.

"That is what got her killed..."

Laura Noppe, Thomas' mother, said she saw Thomas, her only child, put others first. "It bothered me sometimes."

She talked of her daughter's fondness for animals and creatures, even snakes and bugs, called her loving and caring, and made little further comment beyond one returning thought. "She must have seen something in that guy to think she could help him."

cases.name: Virginia May "Virgie" Zwick
cases.about: Her obituary said, "After graduating from Jackson High School she studied to be a beautician and practiced cosmetology for a while then moved on to other endeavors. She became a mother for the first time in 1975 and raised two children. As the children got older, she worked in a few of her father's restaurants, moved on to the accounting department at the local newspaper, and finally settled into an administrative role supporting her husband and brother-in-law's family business. Even at an early age she loved to travel and was fortunate to have visited several countries throughout the world. She always loved a good party and had a mad sense of style. Her sense of humor was legendary; you never knew what she would say next. She was a wonderful mother, sister, and wife."
